```{r}
boxplot_illustration
```

::: {.notes}

Key components:

- Box: Extends from Q1 to Q3 and contains the middle 50% of the observations.
- Median line: Represents the 50th percentile.
- Interquartile range: IQR = Q3−Q1.
- Whiskers: Extend to the extreme observations within below and above Q1 and Q3.

:::

## Histogram

```{r}
# ================================================================
# HISTOGRAM AND DENSITY OF ADJUSTED RETURNS
# Complete interactive Plotly visualization
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(plotly)

# ================================================================
# 1. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

ticker_selected <- dados |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker)
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(ticker) |>
  as.character()

if (
  length(ticker_selected) == 0 ||
  is.na(ticker_selected)
) {
  stop("No valid ticker was found in the dataset.")
}

# ================================================================
# 2. PREPARE THE ADJUSTED RETURNS
# ================================================================

dados_distribution <- dados |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(ref_date),
    !is.na(ret_adjusted_prices),
    is.finite(ret_adjusted_prices)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),
    ref_date = as.Date(ref_date),
    adjusted_return =
      as.numeric(ret_adjusted_prices)
  ) |>
  arrange(ref_date)

n_observations <- nrow(
  dados_distribution
)

if (n_observations < 2) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least two valid observations are required for ",
      ticker_selected,
      "."
    )
  )
}

returns <- dados_distribution$adjusted_return

# ================================================================
# 3. CALCULATE DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
# ================================================================

sample_mean <- mean(
  returns
)

sample_median <- median(
  returns
)

sample_sd <- sd(
  returns
)

minimum_return <- min(
  returns
)

maximum_return <- max(
  returns
)

q01 <- quantile(
  returns,
  probs = 0.01,
  names = FALSE,
  type = 7
)

q25 <- quantile(
  returns,
  probs = 0.25,
  names = FALSE,
  type = 7
)

q75 <- quantile(
  returns,
  probs = 0.75,
  names = FALSE,
  type = 7
)

q99 <- quantile(
  returns,
  probs = 0.99,
  names = FALSE,
  type = 7
)

sample_iqr <- q75 - q25

# ================================================================
# 4. CALCULATE BIN WIDTH
#
# The Freedman-Diaconis rule is used:
#
# bin width = 2 * IQR / n^(1/3)
#
# A fallback based on the data range is used if the IQR is zero.
# ================================================================

bin_width <- 2 *
  sample_iqr /
  (
    n_observations^(1 / 3)
  )

observed_range <- maximum_return -
  minimum_return

if (
  !is.finite(observed_range) ||
  observed_range <= 0
) {
  observed_range <- max(
    abs(maximum_return),
    0.01
  )
}

if (
  !is.finite(bin_width) ||
  bin_width <= 0
) {
  bin_width <- observed_range /
    max(
      10,
      ceiling(
        sqrt(n_observations)
      )
    )
}

if (
  !is.finite(bin_width) ||
  bin_width <= 0
) {
  bin_width <- 0.001
}

number_bins <- ceiling(
  observed_range /
    bin_width
)

number_bins <- max(
  8,
  min(
    number_bins,
    60
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 5. COMPUTE THE HISTOGRAM EXPLICITLY
#
# Calculating the histogram before plotting provides reliable
# tooltips with interval, frequency, proportion, and density.
# ================================================================

histogram_object <- hist(
  returns,
  breaks = number_bins,
  plot = FALSE,
  right = TRUE,
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

histogram_data <- tibble(
  bin_number = seq_along(
    histogram_object$counts
  ),

  lower_bound =
    histogram_object$breaks[
      -length(
        histogram_object$breaks
      )
    ],

  upper_bound =
    histogram_object$breaks[
      -1
    ],

  midpoint =
    histogram_object$mids,

  frequency =
    histogram_object$counts,

  density =
    histogram_object$density
) |>
  mutate(
    bin_width =
      upper_bound -
      lower_bound,

    proportion =
      frequency /
      n_observations,

    interval_label = paste0(
      "(",
      scales::percent(
        lower_bound,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      ", ",
      scales::percent(
        upper_bound,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "]"
    ),

    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Histogram bin</b>",
      "<br>",
      "<span style='color:#64748B'>",
      ticker_selected,
      "</span>",
      "<br><br>",

      "<b>Return interval:</b> ",
      interval_label,
      "<br>",

      "<b>Frequency:</b> ",
      scales::comma(
        frequency
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Sample proportion:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        proportion,
        accuracy = 0.1
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Density:</b> ",
      scales::number(
        density,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br><br>",

      "<span style='color:#475569'>",
      "The area of this bar represents",
      "<br>",
      "the proportion of observations in the interval.",
      "</span>"
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 6. ESTIMATE THE KERNEL DENSITY
#
# adjust = 1 uses R's default bandwidth.
# ================================================================

density_estimate <- density(
  returns,
  n = 1024,
  adjust = 1,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

density_data <- tibble(
  adjusted_return =
    density_estimate$x,

  estimated_density =
    density_estimate$y
) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Kernel density estimate</b>",
      "<br>",
      "<span style='color:#64748B'>",
      ticker_selected,
      "</span>",
      "<br><br>",

      "<b>Adjusted return:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        adjusted_return,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Estimated density:</b> ",
      scales::number(
        estimated_density,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br><br>",

      "<span style='color:#475569'>",
      "The curve is a smoothed estimate",
      "<br>",
      "of the distribution's shape.",
      "</span>"
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 7. ESTIMATE THE MODE FROM THE DENSITY
# ================================================================

mode_index <- which.max(
  density_data$estimated_density
)

estimated_mode <-
  density_data$adjusted_return[
    mode_index
  ]

mode_density <-
  density_data$estimated_density[
    mode_index
  ]

# ================================================================
# 8. OBTAIN DENSITY VALUES AT MEAN AND MEDIAN
# ================================================================

density_at_mean <- approx(
  x = density_data$adjusted_return,
  y = density_data$estimated_density,
  xout = sample_mean,
  rule = 2
)$y

density_at_median <- approx(
  x = density_data$adjusted_return,
  y = density_data$estimated_density,
  xout = sample_median,
  rule = 2
)$y

# ================================================================
# 9. DEFINE THE RUG-PLOT POSITION
# ================================================================

maximum_histogram_density <- max(
  histogram_data$density,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

maximum_kernel_density <- max(
  density_data$estimated_density,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

maximum_density <- max(
  maximum_histogram_density,
  maximum_kernel_density
)

if (
  !is.finite(maximum_density) ||
  maximum_density <= 0
) {
  maximum_density <- 1
}

rug_position <- -0.045 *
  maximum_density

y_min <- -0.085 *
  maximum_density

y_max <- 1.20 *
  maximum_density

# ================================================================
# 10. CREATE OBSERVATION TOOLTIPS
# ================================================================

dados_distribution <- dados_distribution |>
  mutate(
    rug_y = rug_position,

    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>",
      ticker,
      "</b>",
      "<br>",
      "<span style='color:#64748B'>Observed adjusted return</span>",
      "<br><br>",

      "<b>Date:</b> ",
      format(
        ref_date,
        "%d %B %Y"
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Adjusted return:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        adjusted_return,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Distance from mean:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        adjusted_return -
          sample_mean,
        accuracy = 0.001
      )
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 11. DEFINE SAFE X-AXIS LIMITS
#
# Q01 and Q99 are used only to inspect whether the range is being
# dominated by extreme values. All observations remain displayed.
# ================================================================

density_minimum <- min(
  density_data$adjusted_return
)

density_maximum <- max(
  density_data$adjusted_return
)

display_minimum <- min(
  minimum_return,
  density_minimum
)

display_maximum <- max(
  maximum_return,
  density_maximum
)

display_range <- display_maximum -
  display_minimum

if (
  !is.finite(display_range) ||
  display_range <= 0
) {
  display_range <- observed_range
}

x_padding <- 0.04 *
  display_range

x_min <- display_minimum -
  x_padding

x_max <- display_maximum +
  x_padding

# ================================================================
# 12. CREATE TOOLTIP TEXT FOR LOCATION MEASURES
# ================================================================

mean_hover <- paste0(
  "<b>Sample mean</b>",
  "<br><br>",

  "<b>Return:</b> ",
  scales::percent(
    sample_mean,
    accuracy = 0.001
  ),
  "<br><br>",

  "<span style='color:#475569'>",
  "The arithmetic balance point",
  "<br>",
  "of the observed returns.",
  "</span>"
)

median_hover <- paste0(
  "<b>Sample median</b>",
  "<br><br>",

  "<b>Return:</b> ",
  scales::percent(
    sample_median,
    accuracy = 0.001
  ),
  "<br><br>",

  "<span style='color:#475569'>",
  "Approximately 50% of returns",
  "<br>",
  "are at or below this value.",
  "</span>"
)

mode_hover <- paste0(
  "<b>Estimated mode</b>",
  "<br><br>",

  "<b>Return:</b> ",
  scales::percent(
    estimated_mode,
    accuracy = 0.001
  ),
  "<br><br>",

  "<span style='color:#475569'>",
  "The estimated density reaches",
  "<br>",
  "its maximum at this return.",
  "</span>"
)

# ================================================================
# 13. START THE INTERACTIVE PLOT
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- plot_ly()

# ================================================================
# 14. ADD THE HISTOGRAM BARS
#
# The bar heights are densities, ensuring compatibility with
# the kernel-density curve.
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- distribution_plot |>
  add_trace(
    data = histogram_data,

    x = ~midpoint,
    y = ~density,
    width = ~bin_width,
    text = ~hover_text,

    type = "bar",

    name = "Histogram",

    marker = list(
      color = "rgba(47,111,165,0.48)",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 1
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate =
      "%{text}<extra></extra>",

    showlegend = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 15. ADD THE KERNEL-DENSITY CURVE
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- distribution_plot |>
  add_trace(
    data = density_data,

    x = ~adjusted_return,
    y = ~estimated_density,
    text = ~hover_text,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines",

    name = "Kernel density",

    line = list(
      color = "#173F73",
      width = 3,
      shape = "spline",
      smoothing = 0.8
    ),

    hovertemplate =
      "%{text}<extra></extra>",

    showlegend = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 16. ADD OBSERVATIONS AS A RUG PLOT
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- distribution_plot |>
  add_trace(
    data = dados_distribution,

    x = ~adjusted_return,
    y = ~rug_y,
    text = ~hover_text,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    name = "Observed returns",

    marker = list(
      color = "#475569",
      size = 7,
      opacity = 0.32,
      symbol = "line-ns",

      line = list(
        color = "#475569",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate =
      "%{text}<extra></extra>",

    showlegend = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 17. ADD THE SAMPLE MEAN
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- distribution_plot |>
  add_trace(
    x = sample_mean,
    y = density_at_mean,
    text = mean_hover,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    name = "Mean",

    marker = list(
      color = "#DC2626",
      size = 13,
      symbol = "circle",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate =
      "%{text}<extra></extra>",

    showlegend = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 18. ADD THE SAMPLE MEDIAN
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- distribution_plot |>
  add_trace(
    x = sample_median,
    y = density_at_median,
    text = median_hover,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    name = "Median",

    marker = list(
      color = "#059669",
      size = 14,
      symbol = "diamond",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate =
      "%{text}<extra></extra>",

    showlegend = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 19. ADD THE ESTIMATED MODE
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- distribution_plot |>
  add_trace(
    x = estimated_mode,
    y = mode_density,
    text = mode_hover,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    name = "Estimated mode",

    marker = list(
      color = "#D97706",
      size = 13,
      symbol = "square",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate =
      "%{text}<extra></extra>",

    showlegend = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 20. CREATE REFERENCE LINES
# ================================================================

distribution_shapes <- list(

  # Sample mean
  list(
    type = "line",

    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",

    x0 = sample_mean,
    x1 = sample_mean,

    y0 = 0,
    y1 = density_at_mean,

    line = list(
      color = "#DC2626",
      width = 1.5,
      dash = "dot"
    ),

    layer = "above"
  ),

  # Sample median
  list(
    type = "line",

    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",

    x0 = sample_median,
    x1 = sample_median,

    y0 = 0,
    y1 = density_at_median,

    line = list(
      color = "#059669",
      width = 1.5,
      dash = "dash"
    ),

    layer = "above"
  ),

  # Estimated mode
  list(
    type = "line",

    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",

    x0 = estimated_mode,
    x1 = estimated_mode,

    y0 = 0,
    y1 = mode_density,

    line = list(
      color = "#D97706",
      width = 1.5,
      dash = "dot"
    ),

    layer = "above"
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 21. APPLY THE COMPLETE LAYOUT
# ================================================================

distribution_plot <- distribution_plot |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "<b>What Does the Distribution of Returns Look Like?</b>",
        "<br>",
        "<span style='font-size:13px;color:#64748B'>",
        "Histogram and kernel-density estimate for adjusted daily ",
        "returns of ",
        ticker_selected,
        "</span>"
      ),

      x = 0.02,
```

## Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(plotly)

# ================================================================
# 1. DATA PREPARATION
# ================================================================

ticker_selected <- tickers[1]

dados_ecdf <- dados |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(ret_adjusted_prices),
    is.finite(ret_adjusted_prices)
  ) |>
  arrange(ret_adjusted_prices)

n_observations <- nrow(dados_ecdf)

if (n_observations == 0) {
  stop("No valid observations were found for the selected ticker.")
}

# ================================================================
# 2. EMPIRICAL CUMULATIVE DISTRIBUTION
#
# One row for each distinct observed return.
# The probability is the proportion of observations less than or
# equal to that return.
# ================================================================

ecdf_data <- dados_ecdf |>
  count(
    ret_adjusted_prices,
    name = "frequency"
  ) |>
  arrange(ret_adjusted_prices) |>
  mutate(
    cumulative_count = cumsum(frequency),

    cumulative_probability =
      cumulative_count / sum(frequency),

    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>",
      ticker_selected,
      "</b>",
      "<br>",
      "<span style='color:#6B7280'>Empirical cumulative distribution</span>",
      "<br><br>",
      "<b>Daily return:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        ret_adjusted_prices,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br>",
      "<b>Cumulative probability:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        cumulative_probability,
        accuracy = 0.1
      ),
      "<br>",
      "<b>Observations at or below:</b> ",
      scales::comma(cumulative_count),
      " of ",
      scales::comma(sum(frequency)),
      "<br>",
      "<b>Frequency at this exact return:</b> ",
      scales::comma(frequency),
      "<br><br>",
      "<span style='color:#4B5563'>",
      scales::percent(
        cumulative_probability,
        accuracy = 0.1
      ),
      " of observed returns were",
      "<br>less than or equal to ",
      scales::percent(
        ret_adjusted_prices,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      ".</span>"
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 3. SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ================================================================

ecdf_function <- stats::ecdf(
  dados_ecdf$ret_adjusted_prices
)

summary_ecdf <- dados_ecdf |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    minimum = min(
      ret_adjusted_prices
    ),

    maximum = max(
      ret_adjusted_prices
    ),

    probability_non_positive =
      mean(ret_adjusted_prices <= 0),

    q05 = quantile(
      ret_adjusted_prices,
      probs = 0.05,
      names = FALSE
    ),

    median = quantile(
      ret_adjusted_prices,
      probs = 0.50,
      names = FALSE
    ),

    q95 = quantile(
      ret_adjusted_prices,
      probs = 0.95,
      names = FALSE
    )
  )

probability_non_positive <-
  summary_ecdf$probability_non_positive

q05_return <-
  summary_ecdf$q05

median_return <-
  summary_ecdf$median

q95_return <-
  summary_ecdf$q95

q05_probability <-
  as.numeric(ecdf_function(q05_return))

median_probability <-
  as.numeric(ecdf_function(median_return))

q95_probability <-
  as.numeric(ecdf_function(q95_return))

# ================================================================
# 4. DATA FOR THE STEP FUNCTION
#
# The first point starts at probability zero, making the empirical
# nature of the ECDF visually explicit.
# ================================================================

return_range <-
  summary_ecdf$maximum - summary_ecdf$minimum

if (return_range == 0) {
  return_range <- abs(summary_ecdf$maximum)

  if (return_range == 0) {
    return_range <- 0.01
  }
}

x_padding <- 0.05 * return_range

x_min <- summary_ecdf$minimum - x_padding
x_max <- summary_ecdf$maximum + x_padding

ecdf_line_data <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    ret_adjusted_prices = x_min,
    cumulative_probability = 0
  ),
  ecdf_data |>
    select(
      ret_adjusted_prices,
      cumulative_probability
    )
)

# ================================================================
# 5. QUANTILE POINTS
# ================================================================

quantile_points <- tibble(
  measure = c(
    "5th percentile",
    "Median",
    "95th percentile"
  ),

  return = c(
    q05_return,
    median_return,
    q95_return
  ),

  probability = c(
    q05_probability,
    median_probability,
    q95_probability
  ),

  color = c(
    "#D97706",
    "#059669",
    "#7C3AED"
  ),

  symbol = c(
    "circle",
    "diamond",
    "circle"
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>",
      measure,
      "</b>",
      "<br><br>",
      "<b>Return:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        return,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br>",
      "<b>Cumulative probability:</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        probability,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    )
  )

zero_hover_text <- paste0(
  "<b>Non-positive return threshold</b>",
  "<br><br>",
  "<b>Return:</b> 0.000%",
  "<br>",
  "<b>Cumulative probability:</b> ",
  scales::percent(
    probability_non_positive,
    accuracy = 0.1
  ),
  "<br><br>",
  scales::percent(
    probability_non_positive,
    accuracy = 0.1
  ),
  " of observed daily returns",
  "<br>were less than or equal to zero."
)

# ================================================================
# 6. INTERACTIVE PLOT
# ================================================================

ecdf_plot <- plot_ly() |>

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # ECDF step line
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(
    data = ecdf_line_data,

    x = ~ret_adjusted_prices,
    y = ~cumulative_probability,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "lines",

    line = list(
      color = "#173F73",
      width = 3,
      shape = "hv"
    ),

    hoverinfo = "skip",
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Interactive points
  #
  # These points are sufficiently large to create a comfortable
  # hover target, but visually subtle enough not to dominate.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(
    data = ecdf_data,

    x = ~ret_adjusted_prices,
    y = ~cumulative_probability,
    text = ~hover_text,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    marker = list(
      color = "#173F73",
      size = 7,
      opacity = 0.28,

      line = list(
        color = "#173F73",
        width = 0.5
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Probability of a non-positive return
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(
    x = 0,
    y = probability_non_positive,
    text = zero_hover_text,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    name = "Return ≤ 0",

    marker = list(
      color = "#DC2626",
      size = 13,
      symbol = "circle",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
    showlegend = TRUE
  ) |>

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5th percentile
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(
    data = quantile_points |>
      filter(measure == "5th percentile"),

    x = ~return,
    y = ~probability,
    text = ~hover_text,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    name = "5th percentile",

    marker = list(
      color = "#D97706",
      size = 12,
      symbol = "circle",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
    showlegend = TRUE
  ) |>

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Median
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(
    data = quantile_points |>
      filter(measure == "Median"),

    x = ~return,
    y = ~probability,
    text = ~hover_text,

    type = "scatter",
    mode = "markers",

    name = "Median",

    marker = list(
      color = "#059669",
      size = 13,
      symbol = "diamond",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",

  ) |>

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # 95th percentile
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(
    data = quantile_points |>
      filter(measure == "95th percentile"),

    x = ~return,
    y = ~probability,
    text = ~hover_text,

    type = "scatter",

    name = "95th percentile",

    marker = list(
      color = "#7C3AED",

      line = list(
        color = "white",
        width = 2
      )
    ),

    hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
    showlegend = TRUE
  ) |>

  # ==============================================================
  # 7. PROFESSIONAL LAYOUT
  # ==============================================================

  layout(
    title = list(
```

## Correlation Matrix

```{r}
# ================================================================
# CORRELATION MATRIX OF ADJUSTED RETURNS
# Complete interactive heatmap for Data Visualization
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(plotly)

# ================================================================
# 1. PREPARE THE LONG-FORM DATA
#
# If more than one observation exists for the same date and ticker,
# the mean is used to produce one adjusted return per pair.
# ================================================================

dados_correlation_long <- dados |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ref_date),
    !is.na(ticker),
    !is.na(ret_adjusted_prices),
    is.finite(ret_adjusted_prices)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    ref_date = as.Date(ref_date),
    ticker = as.character(ticker),
    ret_adjusted_prices =
      as.numeric(ret_adjusted_prices)
  ) |>
  group_by(
    ref_date,
    ticker
  ) |>
  summarise(
    ret_adjusted_prices =
      mean(
        ret_adjusted_prices,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

if (nrow(dados_correlation_long) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No valid adjusted returns were found in the dataset."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 2. REMOVE TICKERS WITH INSUFFICIENT DATA
#
# At least three observations and positive variability are needed.
# ================================================================

ticker_quality <- dados_correlation_long |>
  group_by(ticker) |>
  summarise(
    valid_observations = n(),
    return_sd = sd(
      ret_adjusted_prices,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(
    valid_observations >= 3,
    !is.na(return_sd),
    is.finite(return_sd),
    return_sd > 0
  )

valid_tickers <- ticker_quality$ticker

if (length(valid_tickers) < 2) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least two tickers with three valid observations ",
      "and positive variance are required."
    )
  )
}

dados_correlation_long <- dados_correlation_long |>
  filter(
    ticker %in% valid_tickers
  )

# ================================================================
# 3. CONVERT THE DATA TO WIDE FORMAT
#
# Each row is a date.
# Each column is one ticker.
# ================================================================

dados_correlation_wide <- dados_correlation_long |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = ticker,
    values_from = ret_adjusted_prices
  ) |>
  arrange(ref_date)

return_matrix <- dados_correlation_wide |>
  select(
    -ref_date
  ) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Guarantee numeric columns

return_matrix[] <- lapply(
  return_matrix,
  as.numeric
)

# Remove any columns that became invalid after widening

valid_columns <- vapply(
  return_matrix,
  function(x) {
    n_valid <- sum(
      is.finite(x)
    )

    x_sd <- sd(
      x,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    n_valid >= 3 &&
      is.finite(x_sd) &&
      x_sd > 0
  },
  logical(1)
)

return_matrix <- return_matrix[
  ,
  valid_columns,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (ncol(return_matrix) < 2) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Fewer than two valid ticker series remained ",
      "after checking missing values and variance."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. CALCULATE THE PEARSON CORRELATION MATRIX
#
# pairwise.complete.obs uses every date available for each pair.
# ================================================================

correlation_matrix <- cor(
  return_matrix,
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

# ================================================================
# 5. CALCULATE THE NUMBER OF MATCHED OBSERVATIONS FOR EACH PAIR
# ================================================================

ticker_names <- colnames(
  return_matrix
)

number_tickers <- length(
  ticker_names
)

pair_count_matrix <- matrix(
  NA_integer_,
  nrow = number_tickers,
  ncol = number_tickers,
  dimnames = list(
    ticker_names,
    ticker_names
  )
)

for (i in seq_len(number_tickers)) {

  for (j in seq_len(number_tickers)) {

    pair_count_matrix[i, j] <- sum(
      is.finite(
        return_matrix[[i]]
      ) &
        is.finite(
          return_matrix[[j]]
        )
    )
  }
}

# ================================================================
# 6. REMOVE PAIRS WITH TOO FEW MATCHED OBSERVATIONS
#
# Correlations with fewer than three matched observations are not
# displayed. This does not impose a statistical significance rule.
# ================================================================

correlation_matrix[
  pair_count_matrix < 3
] <- NA_real_

# Diagonal elements must remain equal to one

diag(
  correlation_matrix
) <- 1

# ================================================================
# 7. ORDER TICKERS BY CORRELATION SIMILARITY
#
# Hierarchical clustering places similarly correlated assets near
# one another, making blocks easier to see.
#
# Missing correlations are set to zero only for constructing the
# ordering distance. The displayed matrix keeps them as NA.
# ================================================================

clustering_correlation <- correlation_matrix

clustering_correlation[
  !is.finite(
    clustering_correlation
  )
] <- 0

clustering_correlation <- pmax(
  pmin(
    clustering_correlation,
    1
  ),
  -1
)

diag(
  clustering_correlation
) <- 1

correlation_distance <- as.dist(
  1 - clustering_correlation
)

ticker_clustering <- hclust(
  correlation_distance,
  method = "average"
)

ticker_order <- ticker_clustering$order

ordered_tickers <- ticker_names[
  ticker_order
]

correlation_matrix_ordered <-
  correlation_matrix[
    ticker_order,
    ticker_order,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

pair_count_matrix_ordered <-
  pair_count_matrix[
    ticker_order,
    ticker_order,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

# ================================================================
# 8. CREATE THE HOVER-TEXT MATRIX
#
# A prebuilt text matrix is more reliable than customdata for
# Plotly tooltips in RStudio Viewer and Quarto.
# ================================================================

hover_matrix <- matrix(
  "",
  nrow = number_tickers,
  ncol = number_tickers,
  dimnames = list(
    ordered_tickers,
    ordered_tickers
  )
)

for (i in seq_len(number_tickers)) {

  for (j in seq_len(number_tickers)) {

    correlation_value <-
      correlation_matrix_ordered[i, j]

    matched_observations <-
      pair_count_matrix_ordered[i, j]

    if (is.finite(correlation_value)) {

      direction_text <- if (
        correlation_value > 0
      ) {
        "Positive linear association"
      } else if (
        correlation_value < 0
      ) {
        "Negative linear association"
      } else {
        "No linear direction"
      }

      strength_text <- if (
        i == j
      ) {
        "Perfect self-correlation"
      } else if (
        abs(correlation_value) >= 0.80
      ) {
        "Very strong"
      } else if (
        abs(correlation_value) >= 0.60
      ) {
        "Strong"
      } else if (
        abs(correlation_value) >= 0.40
      ) {
        "Moderate"
      } else if (
        abs(correlation_value) >= 0.20
      ) {
        "Weak"
      } else {
        "Very weak"
      }

      hover_matrix[i, j] <- paste0(
        "<b>",
        ordered_tickers[j],
        " vs ",
        ordered_tickers[i],
        "</b>",
        "<br><br>",

        "<b>Pearson correlation:</b> ",
        scales::number(
          correlation_value,
          accuracy = 0.01
        ),
        "<br>",

        "<b>Direction:</b> ",
        direction_text,
        "<br>",

        "<b>Descriptive strength:</b> ",
        strength_text,
        "<br>",

        "<b>Matched dates:</b> ",
        scales::comma(
          matched_observations
        ),
        "<br><br>",

        "<span style='color:#475569'>",
        "Correlation describes linear association",
        "<br>",
        "and does not establish causality.",
        "</span>"
      )

    } else {

      hover_matrix[i, j] <- paste0(
        "<b>",
        ordered_tickers[j],
        " vs ",
        ordered_tickers[i],
        "</b>",
        "<br><br>",

        "<b>Correlation:</b> unavailable",
        "<br>",

        "<b>Matched dates:</b> ",
        scales::comma(
          matched_observations
        ),
        "<br><br>",

        "<span style='color:#475569'>",
        "At least three matched observations",
        "<br>",
        "are required in this visualization.",
        "</span>"
      )
    }
  }
}

# ================================================================
# 9. CREATE THE CELL-LABEL MATRIX
#
# Values are displayed only when there are at most 20 tickers.
# For larger matrices, labels would make the heatmap too cluttered.
# ================================================================

show_cell_values <- number_tickers <= 20

cell_label_matrix <- matrix(
  "",
  nrow = number_tickers,
  ncol = number_tickers,
  dimnames = list(
    ordered_tickers,
    ordered_tickers
  )
)

if (show_cell_values) {

  cell_label_matrix <- ifelse(
    is.finite(
      correlation_matrix_ordered
    ),
    sprintf(
      "%.2f",
      correlation_matrix_ordered
    ),
    ""
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 10. CALCULATE GLOBAL SUMMARY VALUES FOR THE ANNOTATIONS
#
# The diagonal is removed because self-correlations are always one.
# ================================================================

upper_triangle_indices <- upper.tri(
  correlation_matrix_ordered,
  diag = FALSE
)

pairwise_correlations <-
  correlation_matrix_ordered[
    upper_triangle_indices
  ]

pairwise_counts <-
  pair_count_matrix_ordered[
    upper_triangle_indices
  ]

valid_pairs <- is.finite(
  pairwise_correlations
)

number_valid_pairs <- sum(
  valid_pairs
)

if (number_valid_pairs > 0) {

  strongest_positive_index <- which.max(
    ifelse(
      valid_pairs,
      pairwise_correlations,
      -Inf
    )
  )

  strongest_negative_index <- which.min(
    ifelse(
      valid_pairs,
      pairwise_correlations,
      Inf
    )
  )

  upper_positions <- which(
    upper_triangle_indices,
    arr.ind = TRUE
  )

  positive_position <-
    upper_positions[
      strongest_positive_index,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

  negative_position <-
    upper_positions[
      strongest_negative_index,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

  strongest_positive_value <-
    correlation_matrix_ordered[
      positive_position[1, 1],
      positive_position[1, 2]
    ]

  strongest_positive_pair <- paste0(
    rownames(
      correlation_matrix_ordered
    )[
      positive_position[1, 1]
    ],
    " and ",
    colnames(
      correlation_matrix_ordered
    )[
      positive_position[1, 2]
    ]
  )

  strongest_negative_value <-
    correlation_matrix_ordered[
      negative_position[1, 1],
      negative_position[1, 2]
    ]

  strongest_negative_pair <- paste0(
    rownames(
      correlation_matrix_ordered
    )[
      negative_position[1, 1]
    ],
    " and ",
    colnames(
      correlation_matrix_ordered
    )[
      negative_position[1, 2]
    ]
  )

} else {

  strongest_positive_value <- NA_real_
  strongest_positive_pair <- "Unavailable"

  strongest_negative_value <- NA_real_
  strongest_negative_pair <- "Unavailable"
}

# ================================================================
# 11. DEFINE A DATA-VISUALIZATION COLOR SCALE
#
# The scale is:
# - symmetric around zero;
# - blue for negative correlation;
# - neutral near zero;
# - red for positive correlation.
#
# zmin and zmax are fixed at -1 and +1, preventing colors from
# changing meaning across different datasets.
# ================================================================

correlation_colors <- list(
  list(
    0.00,
    "#2166AC"
  ),
  list(
    0.25,
    "#67A9CF"
  ),
  list(
    0.50,
    "#F7F7F7"
  ),
  list(
    0.75,
    "#EF8A62"
  ),
  list(
    1.00,
    "#B2182B"
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 12. CREATE THE INTERACTIVE HEATMAP
# ================================================================

correlation_heatmap <- plot_ly(
  x = ordered_tickers,
  y = ordered_tickers,

  z = correlation_matrix_ordered,
  text = hover_matrix,

  type = "heatmap",

  colorscale = correlation_colors,

  zmin = -1,
  zmax = 1,
  zmid = 0,

  xgap = 1,
  ygap = 1,

  hovertemplate =
    "%{text}<extra></extra>",

  colorbar = list(
    title = list(
      text = "Pearson<br>correlation",
      side = "right"
    ),

    tickmode = "array",

    tickvals = c(
      -1,
      -0.5,
      0,
      0.5,
      1
    ),

    ticktext = c(
      "-1.0",
      "-0.5",
      "0.0",
      "0.5",
      "1.0"
    ),

    thickness = 18,

    len = 0.78,

    x = 1.03,

    outlinewidth = 0
  ),

  showscale = TRUE
)

# ================================================================
# 13. ADD CELL VALUES WHEN THE MATRIX IS READABLE
#
# Plotly heatmaps do not automatically choose contrasting text
# colors, so two text layers are used:
#
# - dark labels around zero;
# - white labels for strong correlations.
# ================================================================

if (show_cell_values) {

  label_grid <- expand.grid(
    x = ordered_tickers,
    y = ordered_tickers,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) |>
    mutate(
      correlation = as.vector(
        t(
          correlation_matrix_ordered
        )
      ),

      label = as.vector(
        t(
          cell_label_matrix
        )
      )
    )

  dark_labels <- label_grid |>
    filter(
      is.finite(correlation),
      abs(correlation) < 0.55
    )

  white_labels <- label_grid |>
    filter(
      is.finite(correlation),
      abs(correlation) >= 0.55
    )

  if (nrow(dark_labels) > 0) {

    correlation_heatmap <-
      correlation_heatmap |>
      add_trace(
        data = dark_labels,

        x = ~x,
        y = ~y,
        text = ~label,

        type = "scatter",
        mode = "text",

        textfont = list(
          color = "#172033",
          size = 10
        ),

        hoverinfo = "skip",

        showlegend = FALSE,

        inherit = FALSE
      )
  }

  if (nrow(white_labels) > 0) {

    correlation_heatmap <-
      correlation_heatmap |>
      add_trace(
        data = white_labels,

        x = ~x,
        y = ~y,
        text = ~label,

        type = "scatter",
        mode = "text",

        textfont = list(
          color = "white",
          size = 10
        ),

        hoverinfo = "skip",

        showlegend = FALSE,

        inherit = FALSE
      )
  }
}

# ================================================================
# 14. CREATE THE SUMMARY ANNOTATION
# ================================================================

if (number_valid_pairs > 0) {

  strongest_positive_text <- paste0(
    "<b>Highest correlation:</b> ",
    strongest_positive_pair,
    " (r = ",
    scales::number(
      strongest_positive_value,
      accuracy = 0.01
    ),
    ")"
  )

  strongest_negative_text <- paste0(
    "<b>Lowest correlation:</b> ",
    strongest_negative_pair,
    " (r = ",
    scales::number(
      strongest_negative_value,
      accuracy = 0.01
    ),
    ")"
  )

} else {

  strongest_positive_text <-
    "<b>Highest correlation:</b> unavailable"

  strongest_negative_text <-
    "<b>Lowest correlation:</b> unavailable"
}

# ================================================================
# 15. APPLY THE COMPLETE LAYOUT
# ================================================================

correlation_heatmap <- correlation_heatmap |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "<b>Which Adjusted Returns Move Together?</b>",
        "<br>",
        "<span style='font-size:13px;color:#64748B'>",
        "Pearson correlation matrix for ",
        number_tickers,
        " tickers, ordered by correlation similarity",
        "</span>"
      ),

      x = 0.02,

      xanchor = "left"
    ),

    xaxis = list(
      title = "",

      side = "bottom",

      tickangle = ifelse(
        number_tickers > 10,
        -45,
        0
      ),

      tickfont = list(
        size = ifelse(
          number_tickers > 20,
          8,
          10
        ),
        color = "#334155"
      ),

      showgrid = FALSE,

      showline = FALSE,

      zeroline = FALSE,

      fixedrange = FALSE
    ),

    yaxis = list(
      title = "",

      autorange = "reversed",

      tickfont = list(
        size = ifelse(
          number_tickers > 20,
          8,
          10
        ),
        color = "#334155"
      ),

      showgrid = FALSE,

      showline = FALSE,

      zeroline = FALSE,

      fixedrange = FALSE,

      scaleanchor = ifelse(
        number_tickers <= 30,
        "x",
        NULL
      ),

      scaleratio = 1
    ),

    hovermode = "closest",

    hoverlabel = list(
      bgcolor = "white",

      bordercolor = "#173F73",

      font = list(
        family = "Arial",
        size = 12,
        color = "#0F172A"
      ),

      align = "left",

      namelength = -1
    ),

    margin = list(
      l = ifelse(
        number_tickers > 20,
        120,
        95
      ),

      r = 135,

      t = 125,

      b = ifelse(
        number_tickers > 10,
        155,
        115
      )
    ),

    paper_bgcolor = "white",

    plot_bgcolor = "white",

    font = list(
      family = "Arial",
      color = "#1E293B"
    ),

    showlegend = FALSE,

    annotations = list(

      # ----------------------------------------------------------
      # SCALE INTERPRETATION
      # ----------------------------------------------------------

      list(
        xref = "paper",
        yref = "paper",

        x = 0,
        y = -0.16,

        text = paste0(
          "<span style='color:#2166AC'><b>Negative:</b> ",
          "the returns tend to move in opposite directions</span>",
          " &nbsp;&nbsp; | &nbsp;&nbsp; ",
          "<span style='color:#64748B'><b>Near zero:</b> ",
          "little linear association</span>",
          " &nbsp;&nbsp; | &nbsp;&nbsp; ",
          "<span style='color:#B2182B'><b>Positive:</b> ",
          "the returns tend to move in the same direction</span>"
        ),

        showarrow = FALSE,

        xanchor = "left",

        yanchor = "top",

        font = list(
          size = 10
        ),

        align = "left"
      ),

      # ----------------------------------------------------------
      # STRONGEST AND WEAKEST DIRECTIONAL PAIRS
      # ----------------------------------------------------------

      list(
        xref = "paper",
        yref = "paper",

        x = 0,
        y = -0.25,

        text = paste0(
          strongest_positive_text,
          "<br>",
          strongest_negative_text
        ),

        showarrow = FALSE,

        xanchor = "left",

        yanchor = "top",

        bgcolor =
          "rgba(248,250,252,0.97)",

        bordercolor = "#CBD5E1",

        borderwidth = 1,

        borderpad = 7,

        font = list(
          size = 10,
          color = "#334155"
        ),

        align = "left"
      ),

      # ----------------------------------------------------------
      # TEACHING TAKEAWAY
      # ----------------------------------------------------------

      list(
        xref = "paper",
        yref = "paper",

        x = 0.50,
        y = -0.36,

        text = paste0(
          "<b>A correlation heatmap reveals patterns across many ",
          "pairwise relationships, but each cell still represents ",
          "only a linear association.</b>",
          "<br>",
          "<span style='font-size:10px;color:#64748B'>",
          "Hover over a cell to inspect the correlation and the ",
          "number of matched dates used for that pair.",
          "</span>"
        ),

        showarrow = FALSE,

        xanchor = "center",

        yanchor = "top",

        bgcolor =
          "rgba(248,250,252,0.97)",

        bordercolor = "#CBD5E1",

        borderwidth = 1,

        borderpad = 7,

        font = list(
          size = 11,
          color = "#334155"
        ),

        align = "center"
      )
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 16. CONFIGURE THE INTERACTION
# ================================================================

correlation_heatmap <- correlation_heatmap |>
  config(
    displaylogo = FALSE,

    responsive = TRUE,

    scrollZoom = TRUE,

    toImageButtonOptions = list(
      format = "png",

      filename =
        "adjusted_returns_correlation_heatmap",

      height = max(
        750,
        35 * number_tickers
      ),

      width = max(
        1100,
        35 * number_tickers
      ),

      scale = 2
    ),

    modeBarButtonsToRemove = c(
      "select2d",
      "lasso2d"
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 17. DISPLAY THE HEATMAP
# ================================================================

correlation_heatmap
```

## Lag plots

```{r}
# ================================================================
# LAG PLOTS OF ADJUSTED RETURNS
# Complete interactive visualization for a Data Visualization class
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)

# ================================================================
# 1. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

ticker_selected <- dados |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker)
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(ticker) |>
  as.character()

if (
  length(ticker_selected) == 0 ||
  is.na(ticker_selected)
) {
  stop("No valid ticker was found in the dataset.")
}

# ================================================================
# 2. PREPARE THE ADJUSTED RETURNS
#
# If there is more than one observation for the same date and
# ticker, the mean is used to create one return per date.
# ================================================================

dados_lag <- dados |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(ref_date),
    !is.na(ret_adjusted_prices),
    is.finite(ret_adjusted_prices)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),
    ref_date = as.Date(ref_date),
    adjusted_return = as.numeric(
      ret_adjusted_prices
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    ref_date
  ) |>
  summarise(
    adjusted_return = mean(
      adjusted_return,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(ref_date)

n_observations <- nrow(dados_lag)

if (n_observations < 12) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least 12 valid observations are required for ",
      ticker_selected,
      " to create lag plots up to lag 10."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 3. DEFINE THE LAGS
#
# These are observation lags, not necessarily calendar-day lags.
# For trading data:
#
# lag 1  = previous available trading observation
# lag 5  = five available trading observations earlier
# ================================================================

lags_selected <- c(
  1L,
  2L,
  5L,
  10L
)

# Keep only lags that are possible given the sample size

lags_selected <- lags_selected[
  lags_selected < n_observations
]

if (length(lags_selected) == 0) {
  stop(
    "The dataset does not contain enough observations for a lag plot."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. CREATE THE LAGGED DATA
#
# For each lag k, the graph compares:
#
# x = return at time t-k
# y = return at time t
# ================================================================

lag_plot_data <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    lags_selected,
    function(k) {

      dados_lag |>
        mutate(
          lag_number = k,

          lagged_date = lag(
            ref_date,
            n = k
          ),

          lagged_return = lag(
            adjusted_return,
            n = k
          )
        ) |>
        filter(
          !is.na(lagged_date),
          !is.na(lagged_return),
          is.finite(lagged_return)
        ) |>
        select(
          ticker,
          ref_date,
          adjusted_return,
          lagged_date,
          lagged_return,
          lag_number
        )
    }
  )
)

if (nrow(lag_plot_data) == 0) {
  stop(
    "No valid matched observations were created for the selected lags."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. CALCULATE SUMMARY STATISTICS FOR EACH LAG
# ================================================================

lag_summary <- lag_plot_data |>
  group_by(lag_number) |>
  summarise(
    matched_observations = n(),

    pearson_correlation = cor(
      lagged_return,
      adjusted_return,
      method = "pearson"
    ),

    spearman_correlation = cor(
      lagged_return,
      adjusted_return,
      method = "spearman"
    ),

    regression_slope = coef(
      lm(
        adjusted_return ~ lagged_return
      )
    )[2],

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    relationship_strength = case_when(
      abs(pearson_correlation) >= 0.80 ~
        "Very strong linear dependence",

      abs(pearson_correlation) >= 0.60 ~
        "Strong linear dependence",

      abs(pearson_correlation) >= 0.40 ~
        "Moderate linear dependence",

      abs(pearson_correlation) >= 0.20 ~
        "Weak linear dependence",

      TRUE ~
        "Very weak linear dependence"
    ),

    facet_label = paste0(
      "Lag ",
      lag_number,
      "\n",
      "Pearson r = ",
      sprintf(
        "%.2f",
        pearson_correlation
      ),
      " | Spearman rho = ",
      sprintf(
        "%.2f",
        spearman_correlation
      )
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 6. JOIN PANEL STATISTICS TO THE OBSERVATIONS
# ================================================================

lag_plot_data <- lag_plot_data |>
  left_join(
    lag_summary |>
      select(
        lag_number,
        matched_observations,
        pearson_correlation,
        spearman_correlation,
        relationship_strength,
        facet_label
      ),
    by = "lag_number"
  )

# Preserve the intended lag order

facet_levels <- lag_summary |>
  arrange(lag_number) |>
  pull(facet_label)

lag_plot_data <- lag_plot_data |>
  mutate(
    facet_label = factor(
      facet_label,
      levels = facet_levels
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 7. IDENTIFY LARGE RETURNS FOR VISUAL EMPHASIS
#
# These thresholds are based on the 95th percentile of the
# absolute returns within each lag panel.
# ================================================================

lag_plot_data <- lag_plot_data |>
  group_by(lag_number) |>
  mutate(
    extreme_threshold = quantile(
      pmax(
        abs(adjusted_return),
        abs(lagged_return)
      ),
      probs = 0.95,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),

    observation_type = if_else(
      pmax(
        abs(adjusted_return),
        abs(lagged_return)
      ) >= extreme_threshold,
      "Large absolute return",
      "Regular observation"
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# ================================================================
# 8. CREATE INTERACTIVE TOOLTIPS
# ================================================================

lag_plot_data <- lag_plot_data |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>",
      ticker,
      " | Lag ",
      lag_number,
      "</b>",
      "<br>",
      "<span style='color:#64748B'>Return persistence</span>",
      "<br><br>",

      "<b>Current date, t:</b> ",
      format(
        ref_date,
        "%d %B %Y"
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Current return, r(t):</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        adjusted_return,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br><br>",

      "<b>Lagged date, t−",
      lag_number,
      ":</b> ",
      format(
        lagged_date,
        "%d %B %Y"
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Lagged return, r(t−",
      lag_number,
      "):</b> ",
      scales::percent(
        lagged_return,
        accuracy = 0.001
      ),
      "<br><br>",

      "<b>Pearson correlation:</b> ",
      scales::number(
        pearson_correlation,
        accuracy = 0.01
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Spearman correlation:</b> ",
      scales::number(
        spearman_correlation,
        accuracy = 0.01
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Matched observations:</b> ",
      scales::comma(
        matched_observations
      ),
      "<br>",

      "<b>Classification:</b> ",
      observation_type
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 9. DEFINE COMMON AXIS LIMITS
#
# Equal limits allow the 45-degree line to be interpreted correctly
# and make comparisons across lag panels easier.
# ================================================================

all_returns <- c(
  lag_plot_data$lagged_return,
  lag_plot_data$adjusted_return
)

common_minimum <- min(
  all_returns,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

common_maximum <- max(
  all_returns,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

common_range <- common_maximum -
  common_minimum

if (
  !is.finite(common_range) ||
  common_range == 0
) {
  common_range <- max(
    abs(common_maximum),
    0.01
  )
}

axis_padding <- 0.06 *
  common_range

axis_minimum <- common_minimum -
  axis_padding

axis_maximum <- common_maximum +
  axis_padding

# ================================================================
# 10. BUILD THE COMPLETE FACETED GGPLOT
# ================================================================

lag_ggplot <- ggplot(
  data = lag_plot_data,
  aes(
    x = lagged_return,
    y = adjusted_return,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Zero-reference lines
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    color = "#CBD5E1",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    color = "#CBD5E1",
    linewidth = 0.45
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # 45-degree persistence line
  #
  # Points close to this line have similar current and lagged
  # returns.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0,
    slope = 1,
    color = "#94A3B8",
    linewidth = 0.7,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # All observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    aes(
      color = observation_type,
      size = observation_type,
      alpha = observation_type
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Linear trend
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_smooth(
    aes(
      group = facet_label
    ),
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    color = "#173F73",
    linewidth = 1,
    inherit.aes = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lag panels
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  facet_wrap(
    facets = vars(facet_label),
    ncol = 2,
    scales = "fixed"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Common scales
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(
      accuracy = 0.1
    ),
    limits = c(
      axis_minimum,
      axis_maximum
    )
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(
      accuracy = 0.1
    ),
    limits = c(
      axis_minimum,
      axis_maximum
    )
  ) +

  coord_fixed(
    ratio = 1
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Controlled colors and emphasis
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Regular observation" = "#2F6FA5",
      "Large absolute return" = "#DC2626"
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +

  scale_size_manual(
    values = c(
      "Regular observation" = 2.3,
      "Large absolute return" = 3.8
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +

  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = c(
      "Regular observation" = 0.48,
      "Large absolute return" = 0.90
    ),
    name = NULL
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Titles
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    title = "Do Current Returns Depend on Past Returns?",

    subtitle = paste0(
      "Lag plots of adjusted daily returns for ",
      ticker_selected,
      " | Each panel compares r(t) with r(t−k)"
    ),

    x = "Lagged adjusted return, r(t−k)",

    y = "Current adjusted return, r(t)",

    caption = paste0(
      "Based on ",
      scales::comma(
        n_observations
      ),
      " valid observations. ",
      "Lags refer to previous available observations, ",
      "not necessarily calendar days. ",
      "The dashed diagonal is y = x; the solid line is a linear fit."
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Presentation theme
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#172033"
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "#475569",
      margin = margin(
        b = 13
      )
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B",
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(
        t = 12
      )
    ),

    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#F8FAFC",
      color = "#CBD5E1",
      linewidth = 0.6
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 10.5,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155",
      lineheight = 1.1,
      margin = margin(
        t = 6,
        r = 5,
        b = 6,
        l = 5
      )
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 10.5,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B"
    ),

    panel.grid.major = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      1.0,
      "lines"
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom",

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 9.5,
      color = "#475569"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 12,
      r = 16,
      b = 12,
      l = 16
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 11. CONVERT TO AN INTERACTIVE PLOTLY GRAPH
# ================================================================

lag_plot <- ggplotly(
  lag_ggplot,
  tooltip = "text",
  dynamicTicks = TRUE
)

# ================================================================
# 12. REFINE THE PLOTLY LAYOUT
# ================================================================

lag_plot <- lag_plot |>
  layout(
    hovermode = "closest",

    hoverlabel = list(
      bgcolor = "white",
      bordercolor = "#173F73",

      font = list(
        family = "Arial",
        size = 12,
        color = "#0F172A"
      ),

      align = "left",
      namelength = -1
    ),

    legend = list(
      orientation = "h",

      x = 0,
      y = -0.12,

      xanchor = "left",
      yanchor = "top",

      font = list(
        size = 10,
        color = "#334155"
      )
    ),

    margin = list(
      l = 85,
      r = 35,
      t = 115,
      b = 110
    ),

    paper_bgcolor = "white",
    plot_bgcolor = "white"
  )

# ================================================================
# 13. CONFIGURE THE GRAPH
# ================================================================

lag_plot <- lag_plot |>
  config(
    displaylogo = FALSE,
    responsive = TRUE,
    scrollZoom = TRUE,

    toImageButtonOptions = list(
      format = "png",

      filename = paste0(
        "lag_plots_",
        ticker_selected
      ),

      height = 850,
      width = 1250,
      scale = 2
    ),

    modeBarButtonsToRemove = c(
      "select2d",
      "lasso2d"
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 14. DISPLAY THE GRAPH
# ================================================================

lag_plot
```
